units.title: Expenses
units.intro: Grammar: will, should and might for how sure we are, and groups of words that tell when, why, how or for what purpose (so that, in order to, lest, although).

lessons.title: Modals of inference: will, should, might

cards.title: Modals of inference: will, should, might
rule: These words show **how sure** you are about something. **will** = very sure (about 100%): *Prices **will be** higher next year.*
**should** = I expect it (about 80%): *The bus left Asmara at 7, so it **should be** in Keren by 9.*
**might / may** = maybe (about 50%): *We **might** need more money for the wedding.*
Negative: **won't** = sure it will not happen; **might not** = maybe not. After will / should / might use the plain verb (no *to*): *It might rain* (not *might to rain*).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Where's Ruth?" "She ____ be in the library; she usually studies there after class, but I'm not sure."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The speaker says "I'm not sure".

**Step 2:** might expresses possibility.

**Step 3:** must and will are too certain; can't means impossible.

**Tip:** How sure? will (very sure) → should (expected) → might (maybe). Purpose: to / in order to + verb; so that + subject + verb. lest = so that … not. although + subject + verb; despite + noun or -ing.

cards.title: Step by step: will, should or might?
cards.problem: Complete: (a) Don't worry about the fees – my father ____ pay them; he has already got the money. (b) The bus left Asmara at 7, so it ____ be in Keren by 9. (c) I'm not sure, but prices ____ go down after the harvest.

steps.text: **Step 1: How sure is the speaker?** Look for clue words.
**Step 2: very sure → will.** (a) *he has already got the money* → **will**.
**Step 3: expected (it normally happens) → should.** (b) a normal journey time → **should**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Ruth studied every day for the exam, so she ____ pass easily.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Studying every day makes passing **expected**.

**Step 2:** expected → **should**.

**Step 3:** *can't* and *might not* say the opposite; *mustn't* means not allowed.

**Tip:** How sure? will (very sure) → should (expected) → might (maybe). Purpose: to / in order to + verb; so that + subject + verb. lest = so that … not. although + subject + verb; despite + noun or -ing.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Take an umbrella. It ____ rain this afternoon – the sky is grey, but I'm not sure.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *I'm not sure* = maybe.

**Step 2:** maybe → **might**.

**Step 3:** *will certainly* and *must* are too sure; *can't* = sure it won't.

**Tip:** How sure? will (very sure) → should (expected) → might (maybe). Purpose: to / in order to + verb; so that + subject + verb. lest = so that … not. although + subject + verb; despite + noun or -ing.

cards.title: Adverbial phrases and clauses
rule: An **adverbial** answers *when? where? why? how?* or *for what purpose?* A **phrase** has no subject + verb (*in the morning, to save money, despite the rain*). A **clause** has a subject + verb (*because prices rose, so that we can save, although she earns a lot*).
**Purpose (why you do it):** *to / in order to* + verb; *so that* + subject + can / will: *I walk to school **so that** I can save money.*

**To stop something bad happening:** *so as not to* + verb, or *lest* + subject + (should) + verb (*lest* is formal and means "so that … not"): *Write your expenses down **lest** you **forget** them.*
**Contrast (a surprise):** *although / even though* + subject + verb; *despite / in spite of* + a noun or -ing. Use only **one** linker: ✗ *Although…, but…*

examples.text: She saves money in order to buy a house.
Although he earns little but he saves.
examples.fix: Although he earns little, he saves.

examples.text: Despite having little money, they were happy.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "Although he earns little but he saves."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the linkers.** *Although* and *but* both show contrast.
**Step 2: The rule.** One contrast needs only **one** linker.
**Step 3: Correct it.** *Although he earns little, he saves.* (or: *He earns little, but he saves.*)

cards.answer: Although he earns little, he saves.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: will = very sure, should = expected, might / may = maybe; all + plain verb. Adverbial phrases and clauses tell when, why, how and for what purpose: so that / in order to (purpose), lest / so as not to (to stop something bad), although / despite (contrast).

cards.why: 'In spite of' is followed by a gerund ('having'). 'Although' and 'Though' must be followed by a clause (Subject + Verb).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence contains an adverbial clause of reason?

options.A: We stayed inside because it was raining.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Reason answers "why?".

**Step 2:** "because it was raining" explains why we stayed inside.

**Step 3:** The others show time, place and manner.

**Tip:** How sure? will (very sure) → should (expected) → might (maybe). Purpose: to / in order to + verb; so that + subject + verb. lest = so that … not. although + subject + verb; despite + noun or -ing.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence joins the two ideas correctly?

options.A: The rain was heavy, we decided to stay indoors.
options.B: The rain was heavy we decided to stay indoors.
options.C: The rain was heavy; therefore, we decided to stay indoors.
options.D: Because the rain was heavy, so we decided to stay indoors.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** A joins two full sentences with only a comma – that is a mistake in English. B has nothing between them at all.

**Step 2:** C is correct: a semicolon (;) and *therefore* join the two sentences.

**Step 3:** D uses two joining words (*Because … so …*). Use only one: *Because the rain was heavy, we stayed indoors.*

**Tip:** Two full sentences cannot be joined with only a comma. Use a full stop, a semicolon (;) or one joining word (and, but, so, because).

**In Tigrinya:** ክልተ ናጻ ዝኾኑ ምሉእ ሓሳባት (independent clauses) ብኮማ ጥራይ ከተኣሳሰሩ ኣይኽእሉን እዮም (እዚ Comma Splice ይበሃል)። ኣብ Option C ዝተጠቐስናሉ ሰሚኮለን (;) ንሰንሰለት ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብግቡእ ይዓጽዎ። Option D ድማ 'Because' ን 'so' ን ብሓባር ብምጥቃም ዝተገብረ ልሙድ ናይ ትርጉም ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Complete with the correct word order: 'The school principal ________.'

options.A: yesterday welcomed the new students warmly
options.B: warmly welcomed the new students yesterday
options.C: welcomed yesterday warmly the new students
options.D: the new students welcomed warmly yesterday

cards.why:
**Step 1:** English order: who + does what + to whom/what + when.

**Step 2:** The how-word *warmly* can stand just before the verb (*warmly welcomed*); the time word *yesterday* goes at the end.

**Step 3:** D puts the object before the verb (Tigrinya order); A and C put words in unusual places. Answer: B.

**Tip:** English order: who? (subject) + does what? (verb) + what? (object) + how? + where? + when?

**In Tigrinya:** ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ናይ ግዜ ተወሳኺ ሓበሬታ (Adverb of Time - 'yesterday') ወትሩ ኣብ መወዳእታ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክስራዕ ከሎ፡ ናይ ኣገባብ ተወሳኺ ሓበሬታ (Adverb of Manner - 'warmly') ድማ ቅድሚ እቲ ዋና ግሲ ይመጽእ። Option B ነዚ ናይ S-V-O ስርዓት ብትኽክል ዝሓለወ እዩ።

glossary.meaning: A part of a sentence with its own subject and verb that tells when, why, how or for what purpose: because prices rose; so that I can save.
